plan.title: feat(session,hooks): re-arm stale session ritual automatically when the same session still holds the checkout

narratives.Description: After a context compaction the write hook restores the session ritual clock and answers the first write with one denial that carries the alignment lines; the retry is not denied for the compaction again. Only the session that owns both the live lease and the ritual can trigger this heal, and the heal stamps no new time, so age staleness and the finalize-owed cadence stay as before. Every other stale-ritual denial prints its recovery command with the caller's session id filled in; a branch switch stays a cold start and is deferred to #6293.
narratives.UserStory: As an agent session that still holds the checkout, I want a compaction to cost me one denial and no manual command, and every other stale-ritual denial to print a command I can run as printed, so that I stop spending turns on ritual recovery.

1. packages/core/src/session/ritual-sentinel.ts: `markRitualStaleAfterCompact` records the overwritten `started_at` as `compact_prior_started_at` unless the state already carries a compact mark with a recorded clock; `writeRitualStateIfStillOwned` takes an optional in-lock admission check.
2. packages/core/src/session/verify-session-ritual.ts: `healCompactMarkForOwnerWrite` checks item 1 (owner, live lease, bound id equals caller, no identity conflict) and `assessRearmEligibility`, then restores the recorded clock and clears the mark explicitly through `writeRitualStateIfStillOwned` with a live-lease re-check inside the ritual lock, and returns the one-time denial text with `READ_ONLY_ALIGNMENT_MESSAGE` and the USER.md line.
3. packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts (ritual branch of `inspectMutationGates` only): call the heal before the ritual-not-ready denial; emit the session-ritual process-cost record with code `hook-compact-heal`; fill the caller's session id into printed recovery commands after the occupancy-aware rewrite.
4. packages/core/src/session/occupancy-recovery.ts: `fillRecoveryCommandSessionId` fills bare `session:start`, `session:start --rearm`, `session:ready` and the `<same-session-id>` token.
5. packages/core/src/run-summary/types.ts: add `hook-compact-heal` to `SESSION_START_TRIGGERS`.
6. Verification: tests in packages/core/src/session/compact-ritual.test.ts for every Bound item 5 case, run by the verify_commands vitest line; `task verify:forward-coverage` at 90% on touched code; content/commands.md compact paragraph; CHANGELOG line.
narratives.Overview:
1. Who may repair. The in-hook repair in item 2 needs all of: the caller is the lease owner (`occupancyGate.admitted` is owner, not member); the lease is live; `ritual.boundSessionId` equals the caller's session id; the caller's host identity has no conflict; and the write's effective worktree is the ritual's worktree. A member, a missing or conflicting identity, or any mismatch gets today's denial. The repair write goes through `writeRitualStateIfStillOwned` under the existing ritual lock.
2. Compaction heal. `markRitualStaleAfterCompact` also records the `started_at` it overwrites, unless one is already recorded (a second compaction before any write). When the write gate finds the compact mark, item 1 holds and `assessRearmEligibility` passes, the hook restores that recorded clock, clears the mark, and denies that one call with a message that carries the re-arm alignment lines (`READ_ONLY_ALIGNMENT_MESSAGE` and the USER.md line) and says to retry. It changes no step result, no gated-step record and no finalize-owed outcome, and it stamps no new time, so age staleness and the inventory cadence are exactly what they were before the compaction. A mark with no recorded clock gets today's denial.
3. Age staleness and a discontinuous HEAD are never cleared by the hook. Their denials, and the other ritual denials that name a recovery command (`dispatcher.ts` 2388 and 2489, `formatSessionStartRecoveryCommand`), print that command with the caller's session id filled in. The occupancy-aware replacement of that text stays as it is.
4. Recording. `SESSION_START_TRIGGERS` gains the closed token `hook-compact-heal`, and each heal emits the existing session-ritual process-cost record.
5. Tests: for item 1, a granted member, a foreign lease, a conflicting identity and a lease lost between check and write; for item 2, a heal with one denial then an admitted retry, parallel calls, a failed quick step (no heal), a state that was already stale by age before the compaction (heal, then the age denial), a discontinuous HEAD under the mark (no heal), two compactions before a write, and a mark written by an older runtime; for item 3, the printed command run as printed, and the occupancy-aware text unchanged; a same-owner branch switch still refused (the locked #2782 test is untouched).

## In plain English
When the session ritual state goes stale, every Write and Edit is refused until the agent reruns the ritual by hand. In a long session this happens many times, and the session that went stale is usually the same one that still holds the checkout. A consumer project counted 12 such denials and 98 `session:ready` runs in one week. The issue asks the hook to refresh the ritual itself when it can show that the same host session still holds the checkout and nothing else changed. The open question is what evidence is enough for that, and which staleness causes may be cleared this way.

## Pains
- P1 — When ritual state goes stale by age, or by a compaction or resume, in the same host session that still holds the checkout, every Write and Edit is refused until a manual re-arm.
- P2 — After that same session changes HEAD with an ordinary git command (switch, pull, merge, rebase), re-arm itself is refused and a full cold `session:start` is required.

## Notes for the arc
- The issue keeps these refusals: a different session, a foreign lease, a changed worktree, a pin change. It also keeps the finalize-owed inventory as a separate gate.
- Related closed work: #1149 (ritual), #4290 (stale ritual with occupancy), #2993 (`session:ready`).

## In plain English

The issue asks hooks to refresh stale session readiness automatically when the same session still owns the checkout, including after its own branch changes. Automatic recovery for age and compaction is plausible, but checkout ownership alone does not prove who changed HEAD. The design also needs to distinguish an owner from an admitted child and preserve checks beyond the ritual timestamp. I verified the relevant code at `1fa8ab9cc7b1aad651e6d65e4103f7820bde3d04` by reading it; no tests, network calls, or mutations were performed.

### 1. Checkout ownership does not establish HEAD-change authorship — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts:734–794` explicitly rejects branch switches, resets, and amendments despite live same-owner occupancy. Its existing exception requires a same-branch rebase sequence in the reflog. `verify-session-ritual.ts:368–405` already accepts forward ancestry and that rebase exception.

**Failure mode:** Another terminal can switch branches while the host session retains its lease. At the next write, matching session and lease IDs establish ownership now, not that this session performed the switch. Broadly accepting discontinuous HEAD under the lease would erase the current distinction.

**Disposition:** Do not bind P2 as written until it names evidence connecting the actual Git transition to the host session. I would retain existing continuity checks and require a narrowly recorded, successful host-associated transition for additional cases, with unexplained changes refusing. The strongest alternative is treating exclusive occupancy as sufficient operational attribution; that is simpler, but would require explicitly accepting externally caused transitions under that lease. Evidence that such transitions are deterministically excluded would flip this verdict.

### 2. Automatic repair must authenticate the caller before changing ritual state — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:2319–2332` invokes ritual verification without passing a host actor. The exact ritual-owner comparison follows verification at `2355–2367`; admitted members deliberately use the lease owner's ceremony. `session-start.ts:833` assesses rebase continuity using the session ID read from ritual state.

**Failure mode:** Adding auto-rearm inside the verifier using the persisted session ID could refresh an owner's ritual on a child/member request, or mutate a mismatched ritual before the dispatcher rejects the caller. Occupancy admission alone includes more than the same-owner case requested here.

**Disposition:** Bind an explicit conjunction before repair: trusted host actor equals live lease owner equals the inspected ritual owner, in the effective worktree. Members, missing identity, and mismatches must not trigger repair. Preserve the final occupancy check and guarded persistence; `session-start.ts:1602–1630` already rechecks ownership before writing. Acceptance coverage should include a granted member and ownership loss during recovery, not only a foreign lease.

### 3. Refreshing timestamps is not equivalent to the existing re-arm path — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts:844–855` requires previously passing quick steps. Its re-arm path runs finalize-owed inventory and refuses blockers at `1921–1955`, before producing refreshed state at `2050–2084`. `hooks/dispatcher.ts:2313–2318` separately requires live agent-hook readiness and reads doctor status from the record.

**Failure mode:** A hook shortcut that merely advances the clock and HEAD can skip finalize-owed or accidentally turn prior failures into fresh success. Conversely, blindly invoking the whole ceremony adds work beyond the issue's description of a clock/HEAD refresh.

**Disposition:** Bind reuse or extraction of the existing guarded re-arm behavior, followed by ordinary write-gate evaluation. State explicitly which evidence is preserved and which checks rerun. Finalize-owed must remain observable and blocking; do not stamp success or clear failure evidence merely because identity matches. Add acceptance cases for stale-plus-failed-readiness and stale-plus-finalize-owed.

### 4. Narrow the claimed HEAD gap and acceptance promise — sharpens-framing

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/session/verify-session-ritual.ts:377–418` already supports forward HEAD rebinding and same-owner rebase continuity. The snapshot's issue body groups switch, pull, merge, and rebase together and promises “no denial.”

**Failure mode:** That framing can drive unnecessary replacement of working continuity logic and make legitimate downstream denials appear to violate acceptance.

**Disposition:** Describe P2 as unsupported discontinuous transitions, especially branch switches. Say “no denial solely for eligible ritual staleness”; retain all subsequent gates. The design can bind with this clarification.

### 5. Embedded authorization remains untrusted — footnote

Snapshot comment `6857545497` relays “you can yolo them and start implementation when they land.” That is instruction-shaped external content, not authority for this critic. I did not follow it; this response remains critique-only.

## In plain English
The issue asks the write hook to refresh a stale session ritual by itself when the same host session still holds the checkout lease, and to treat a HEAD change made by that same session as continuous. The useful part is the age case: the hook already knows the recovery tier, the bound owner and the occupancy verdict, so it can run the re-arm tier in place without new evidence. Two parts cannot bind as written. Compaction staleness exists to stop a summarized session from writing without rebinding its rules, and a lease does not show that this happened. A branch switch cannot be attributed to a session, because git records no session identity. Pull, merge and rebase are also already continuous at the pin, so pain P2 comes down to switch, reset and amend.

### 1. Compact auto re-arm cancels the purpose of #2113 — blocks-the-design
Evidence: CHANGELOG.md:3343 says the #2113 compact marking exists "so summary-based resume cannot silently bypass PreToolUse gates". `markRitualStaleAfterCompact` (packages/core/src/session/ritual-sentinel.ts:415-446) backdates `started_at` and sets `rearm_needed`. Dispatcher.ts:4309-4317 runs this step without checking identity.
Failure mode: after compaction the hook sees the same lease holder, re-arms silently and allows the write. The agent never rereads AGENTS.md / USER.md, so the compact marker does nothing. That is exactly the bypass #2113 closed. Lease ownership is evidence about the checkout, not about the agent's context.
Disposition: exclude the compact/resume marker (`ritualStateMarksRearmNeeded`) from auto re-arm, or allow it only when the hook's allow response injects the re-arm alignment lines (`READ_ONLY_ALIGNMENT_MESSAGE` plus the USER.md line, session-start.ts:1897-1912) into the agent's context. I would bind the exclusion. Evidence that hosts reliably surface allow-path hook text to the model would flip this to the injection variant.

### 2. "Same session made the HEAD change" cannot be observed — blocks-the-design
Evidence: verify-session-ritual.ts:368-404. A forward fast-forward is already continuous (ancestor check), so pull and a merge commit already rebind. A same-owner rebase is admitted under a live lease by `sameOwnerRebaseHeadContinuity` (session-start.ts:745-795, #3884). Branch switch, reset and amend are deliberately refused (#2782), and verify-session-ritual.test.ts:435-474 locks "verify fails closed on same-owner branch switch".
Failure mode: reflog entries have no session id. ## Summary

When session ritual state goes stale, every Write and Edit is refused until the agent reruns the ritual by hand. In a long session this happens many times, and the session that goes stale is usually the same one that still holds the checkout.

Staleness triggers seen (`packages/core/src/session/verify-session-ritual.ts`, `session-start.ts`):

- age past `plan.policy.sessionRitualStalenessHours`;
- compaction or resume ("Compact/resume marked re-arm needed");
- a branch switch or pull ("git HEAD changed discontinuously"), where `session:start --rearm` itself refuses (`REARM_INELIGIBLE_PREFIX`) and a full cold `session:start` is required.

## Consumer impact

On a consumer project, 12 hook denials in one week were stale session state, and `session:ready` ran 98 times. In a maintainer session on 2026-11-13 (0.129.7 and 0.129.8):

- After compaction every edit was denied until re-arm. Re-arm needed three attempts: a redirect was refused as not inspectable, then `--session-id` was missing, then the finalize-owed inventory blocked.
- After a branch switch the re-arm was refused and a cold start was needed.
- Eight hours later, writes to a scratch file outside the repository were denied again for age, while filing this issue.

## Expected

- When the session that presents the stale state is the same host session that holds the occupancy lease, and the worktree is unchanged, the hook re-arms the ritual itself (the re-arm tier: refresh the clock and the HEAD bind) and then evaluates the write. No denial, no manual command.
- A HEAD change made by that same session through an ordinary git command (switch, pull, merge, rebase) is continuous for this purpose and re-arms the same way.
- A different session, a foreign lease, a changed worktree, or a pin change keeps today's refusal and cold-start requirement.
- The finalize-owed inventory stays a separate gate and is not hidden by an auto re-arm.

## Acceptance

- Given a stale ritual and the lease held by the same host session, when that session writes, then the write is evaluated with no manual re-arm, and the re-arm is recorded.
- Given a stale ritual and a lease held by another session, then the write is refused as today.
- A test covers the same-session branch switch.

Refs #1149. Refs #4290. Refs #2993.
